lessons.title: Definition, core and boundaries of direct and reported speech
lessons.meta: Preserve exact words or rebuild meaning from a new reporting viewpoint
examples: Mia said, "I will call you tomorrow."
Mia said that she would call me the next day.
Leo refused to leave.
The teacher asked us to wait.

analyses.text: that she would call me the next day.
analyses.label: that-clause as reported content object

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I, you and tomorrow are anchored to Mia’s speech situation, so direct speech preserves both wording and viewpoint.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I→she, you→me, will→would and tomorrow→the next day shift together because the report is made from a new viewpoint.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Reported speech may summarize the refusal with refused; quotation marks would instead claim the exact words.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: asked us to wait identifies requester, addressee and action; choosing this frame comes before smaller tense or person adjustments.

rules: Direct speech preserves the original wording as an independent utterance; quotation marks also preserve the original speaker’s viewpoint.
Reported speech embeds the meaning in a new reporting sentence; its core is rebuilding speaker, addressee, time and place, not replacing words mechanically.

The boundary is whether exact wording is claimed: direct quotation requires accurate wording and punctuation, while reported speech may preserve meaning and communicative function without copying every word.
Before transforming, identify the communicative type; statements, questions, commands, requests, suggestions and exclamations require different reporting verbs and frames.

questions.question: Which part preserves Mia’s original words and viewpoint?
questions.correct: Inside the quotation, I, tomorrow and you are anchored to Mia’s original speech situation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Inside the quotation, I, tomorrow and you are anchored to Mia’s original speech situation.

questions.question: Which correctly reports Mia’s words later to the original addressee?

options.text: Mia said that I would call you tomorrow.
Mia said that she would call me the next day.

questions.correct: she, me and the next day are resolved from the new reporting viewpoint.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: she, me and the next day are resolved from the new reporting viewpoint.

questions.question: How can Leo’s words be reported by communicative function?
questions.correct: refused to leave preserves the refusal without claiming exact wording.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: refused to leave preserves the refusal without claiming exact wording.

questions.question: Which frame should be chosen first for the request “Please wait”?
questions.correct: Please wait functions as a request, so it does not mechanically take a that-clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Please wait functions as a request, so it does not mechanically take a that-clause.

narration.text:
转告别人的话，有两种做法。一种像把录音原样播放，另一种只把意思准确转述。Mia said, "I will call you tomorrow." 保留了米娅当时的原话，引号里的 I、you 和 tomorrow 都要站在她说话的现场理解，这叫直接引语。<#0.8#>
Mia said that she would call me the next day 则站到新的报告现场。主干是 Mia said，that 后面装的是转述内容。I 原来指米娅，所以变 she；you 指现在的转述者，所以变 me；tomorrow 从后来的时间回看，成为 the next day；will 也变成 would。变化不是为了套表，而是人物和时间坐标真的换了。<#0.8#>
Leo refused to leave 更进一步：它不假装逐字复制，只用 refused 概括“拒绝离开”这个交际功能。The teacher asked us to wait 也先判断原话是请求，再用 ask 加人加 to do。实际转换时，先认清原话是在陈述、提问、命令还是请求；再选择报告动词和骨架；最后核对人称、时态、时间、地点是否因报告现场变化而需要调整。

lessons.title: Direct quotation form and punctuation
lessons.meta: Quotation marks, commas, question marks and capitalization
examples: Mia said, "I am tired."
Tom said, "We are ready."
She asked, "Are you ready?"

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: To report indirectly, remove quotation marks and then adjust person and tense.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The quotation retains its own capitalization and closing punctuation.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: In indirect reporting the question mark disappears because the whole sentence becomes declarative.

rules: Direct quotation preserves the speaker’s exact words and marks them with quotation marks.
With the reporting clause first, normally use a comma after said and capitalize the quotation.
When the quotation is a question or exclamation, put ? or ! inside the quotation marks and do not add a full stop.

questions.question: Which preserves the exact words?

options.text: Mia said that she was tired.

questions.correct: The quoted words are exact.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The quoted words are exact.

questions.question: Which is punctuated correctly?
questions.correct: Use a comma and capitalize the quotation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use a comma and capitalize the quotation.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.correct: The question mark closes the quotation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The question mark closes the quotation.

narration.text:
直接引语的引号像一个清楚的边框：边框里面是说话人原封不动的话，边框外面是“谁说的”。Mia said, "I am tired." 中，Mia said 是报告语，I am tired 是米娅的原话。said 后用逗号把报告语送进引语，引语的 I 仍然大写，句号放在引号里面。<#0.8#>
Tom said, "We are ready." 也是同一结构。引号里的话仍是一句独立句子，所以保留自己的首字母大写和句末标点。不要写成 Tom said "we are ready"，因为这样既丢了报告语后的分隔，也破坏了原话的句子边界。<#0.8#>
原话是问句时，看 She asked, "Are you ready?"。问号属于原问句，因此留在引号内，而且问号已经结束这段引语，外面不再叠加句号。检查直接引语时，只看三个位置：引号是否完整包住原话；报告语后是否有合适的逗号或冒号；原话自己的句号、问号或感叹号是否放在引号内。

lessons.title: The basic reported-speech frame
lessons.meta: Reporting clause + linker + reported content
examples: Mia said that she was tired.
He asked whether I agreed.
The teacher told us that the test was easy.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Remove quotation marks and transform the content into that she was tired.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: A yes-no question cannot mechanically take that; use whether/if.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The quotation becomes the content object after tell us.

rules: Indirect speech removes quotation marks and embeds the content under a reporting clause.
First identify the original sentence type, then choose the linker and word order.
Analyse elements in the new embedded sentence, not by the old quotation boundary.

questions.question: Which is indirect speech?

options.text: Mia said that she was tired.

questions.correct: The content is an object clause of said.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The content is an object clause of said.

questions.question: What should “Do you agree?” first be classified as?
questions.correct: It takes a yes/no answer, so use whether/if.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It takes a yes/no answer, so use whether/if.

questions.question: What does the whole that-clause function as?
questions.correct: us is recipient and the that-clause is the content.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: us is recipient and the that-clause is the content.

narration.text:
间接引语不是给原话换几个单词，而是把原话变成报告动词后面的一个内容模块。Mia said that she was tired 中，Mia said 是报告主干，that she was tired 整体回答“说了什么”，所以是 said 的宾语从句。引号已经去掉，she 和 was 都按新的报告视点组织。<#0.8#>
但不同原句不能都塞进 that。He asked whether I agreed 来自一般疑问，原来的任务是问“同不同意”，因此用 whether 或 if 引出转述内容；放进 asked 后，语序回到 I agreed，不再保留疑问倒装。<#0.8#>
The teacher told us that the test was easy 又多了一个接收者。us 是老师告诉的人，that 从句是老师告诉的内容。于是选择骨架时先问原话是什么句型，再问是否要交代听话人：陈述内容常用 say 加 that 从句；一般疑问用 ask 加 if 或 whether；tell 常先接人，再接内容。骨架选对以后，才处理时态和人称。

lessons.title: Reporting statements with that
lessons.meta: that may be omitted, but statement order remains
examples: Leo said that he needed help.
She said she was busy.
He said he was tired and that he would leave.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: “I need help” becomes that he needed help with person and tense adjusted.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: She said that she was busy can reduce to She said she was busy.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The quotation can be reported as two coordinated that-clauses.

rules: Statements are normally reported with a that-clause.
In speech and informal writing, that is often omitted if the clause boundary remains clear.
With coordinated that-clauses, retaining later that often prevents boundary ambiguity.

questions.question: Report the sentence.

options.text: Leo said that he needed help.
Leo asked if he needed help.

questions.correct: The original is a statement, so use that.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The original is a statement, so use that.

questions.question: Is “She said she was busy” correct?
questions.correct: that may be omitted here after say.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: that may be omitted here after say.

questions.question: What should be retained to clarify the second reported clause?
questions.correct: The later that marks the second coordinated object clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The later that marks the second coordinated object clause.

narration.text:
陈述句的任务是告诉别人一件事，所以转述时最自然的容器是 that 从句。Leo said that he needed help 中，that 后面完整交代“他需要帮助”。原话里的 I 指 Leo，转成 he；在过去的 said 后，need 按这个报告视点写成 needed。<#0.8#>
口语里，that 有时可以不说。She said she was busy 就是省略连接词后的形式，意思不变，因为 said 后面的内容边界很清楚。省略连接词不等于省略从句，也不能把后面的主谓结构改成疑问语序。<#0.8#>
多个内容并列时，边界更容易混。He said he was tired and that he would leave 中，第一个 that 可以省，第二个 that 保留，读者就能立即知道 and 后仍是 said 的另一项内容，而不是前一个从句内部随意接出的成分。处理陈述转述时，先搭 said 加 that 从句；边界清楚时可省 that；内容较长或多个从句并列时，保留后面的 that 会更清楚。

lessons.title: Patterns with say, tell and reporting verbs
lessons.meta: say + content; tell + person + content
examples: Mia said that she was ready.
Mia told me that she was ready.
They talked about the plan.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Mia said to me... becomes Mia told me that... or Mia said to me that....

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: In told me that..., me is the recipient and the that-clause is the content; this does not exclude direct objects such as the truth.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: about the plan marks the topic of conversation; use a say/tell content frame for the actual words or message.

rules: say normally takes content directly; use say to + person for the addressee.
When tell reports specific content, it normally uses tell + person + content; structures such as tell the truth/a story directly name what is told.
speak/talk commonly describe the act or interaction and cannot mechanically replace say/tell before reported content.

questions.question: Which is correct?

options.text: Mia said that she was ready.
Mia said me that she was ready.

questions.correct: say does not directly take a person object.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: say does not directly take a person object.

questions.question: Mia ___ me that she was ready.
questions.correct: The addressee me follows tell and the that-clause gives the content.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The addressee me follows tell and the that-clause gives the content.

questions.question: Which means “They discussed the plan in conversation”?
questions.correct: talk about uses a prepositional phrase to introduce the topic.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: talk about uses a prepositional phrase to introduce the topic.

narration.text:
say 和 tell 都与“说”有关，但它们安排听话人的方式不同。Mia said that she was ready 重点是她说了什么，said 后直接接内容。如果一定要交代对谁说，要在 say 后加介词再接听话人，不能让 say 直接接人。<#0.8#>
Mia told me that she was ready 则把接收者 me 直接放在 told 后面，再接 that 内容从句。这里 me 是听话人，后面的从句是被告知的内容。tell 虽然常接人，但也有“讲真话”这样的直接宾语结构，所以不要把“tell 后永远只能是人”背成死规则。<#0.8#>
They talked about the plan 说的是双方围绕计划交谈，about the plan 是话题，不是某一句被转述的具体内容。选择动词时先看交流方式：只报告一句内容，用 say；强调告诉谁，用 tell 加人；表示双方交谈，用 talk，并用 about 标话题。动词换了，后面的结构也要跟着换，不能把中文一个“说”字套进同一骨架。

lessons.title: Reporting yes-no questions
lessons.meta: ask + if/whether + statement order
examples: She asked if I was ready.
He asked whether Tom had left.
They discussed whether to leave.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Are you ready? becomes if I was ready, removing question inversion.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Had Tom left? becomes whether Tom had left by restoring statement order.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Should we leave? can be compressed into whether to leave after discussed.

rules: Report yes-no questions with ask + if/whether, not that.
An indirect question uses subject + predicate statement order, with no inversion.
whether can pair with or not and is normally used after a preposition or before an infinitive rather than if.

questions.question: Report the question.

options.text: She asked if I was ready.
She said that was I ready.

questions.correct: Use if and restore statement order.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use if and restore statement order.

questions.question: Which word order is correct?
questions.correct: An indirect question uses Tom had left.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: An indirect question uses Tom had left.

questions.question: discussed ___ to leave
questions.correct: Use whether before an infinitive.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use whether before an infinitive.

narration.text:
一般疑问句只需要回答“是”或“不是”。转述时，这个二选一的感觉要保留，但问句外形要收起来。She asked if I was ready 中，if 表示答案尚未确定；原来的直接问句不再倒装，主语回到谓语前。<#0.8#>
He asked whether Tom had left 也是同样逻辑。原问句把助动词放在 Tom 前面，嵌入 asked 后恢复 Tom 在前、had 在后的陈述语序。whether 与 if 都能引出一般疑问转述，whether 在较正式或需要明确“是否”时尤其常见。<#0.8#>
They discussed whether to leave 展示了另一种简洁形式。讨论的主语与行动承担者明确时，“我们是否离开”可以压缩成页面里的不定式结构。检查这类句子时，不要留下问号和倒装：先用 if 或 whether 保留“是否”，再把主语放回助动词前；条件合适时，还可以压缩为“是否加不定式”。

lessons.title: Reporting wh-questions
lessons.meta: Keep the wh-word and use statement order
examples: She asked where I lived.
He asked why she left.
They asked who broke the window.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Where do you live? becomes where I lived, retaining where.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Why did she leave? becomes why she left, removing did and inversion.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Embed Who broke the window after asked, adjusting only context-dependent person and tense.

rules: Keep the original wh-word when reporting a wh-question.
A reported wh-question uses statement order, and do/does/did support disappears.
When the wh-word is subject, the original already has subject-predicate order, so no extra reordering is needed.

questions.question: What is retained when reporting the question?
questions.correct: Keep where; do not add if.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Keep where; do not add if.

questions.question: Report the question.
questions.correct: did disappears and left carries past tense.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: did disappears and left carries past tense.

questions.question: Report the question.
questions.correct: who is subject, so do not add did.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: who is subject, so do not add did.

narration.text:
特殊疑问句已经自带信息缺口，所以转述时保留原来的疑问词，不再加 if 或 whether。She asked where I lived 中，where 继续表示“哪里”，原问句里的助动词消失，语序恢复为主语在前。asked 已经承担提问功能，里面不用再摆出问句外形。<#0.8#>
He asked why she left 展示同样变化。why 保留，原问句中的 did 只是帮助形成疑问，进入从句后去掉，left 放在主语 she 后面。<#0.8#>
They asked who broke the window 看起来没有明显变序，因为 who 本身就是原问句的主语，后面直接接 broke。这不是例外口诀，而是原句本来就是“疑问词作主语”的顺序。转换时先保留 where、why、who 等疑问词，再检查它在从句中做什么；如果原句用了 do、does、did 或倒装，要恢复陈述语序；如果疑问词本身作主语，就不要凭感觉再加助动词。

lessons.title: Reporting commands, requests and imperatives
lessons.meta: tell/ask/order + person + (not) to do
examples: The teacher told us to sit down.
She asked me to help her.
He warned me not to touch it.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The understood subject you refers to the addressees; in the report, us is the object and to sit down states their required action.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Please help me becomes asked me to help her, changing original me to her.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Don’t touch it becomes warned me not to touch it; don’t becomes not to.

rules: A command is commonly reported with tell/order + person + to do.
A polite request commonly uses ask + person + to do, not if as a yes-no question.
A negative imperative uses tell/ask/order + person + not to do, with not before to.

questions.question: Report the command.

options.text: The teacher told us to sit down.
The teacher asked whether we sat down.

questions.correct: A command identifies an addressee and action, so use tell + person + to do.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A command identifies an addressee and action, so use tell + person + to do.

questions.question: Report the request.

options.text: She asked if I help her.
She asked me to help her.

questions.correct: A please-request uses ask sb to do.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A please-request uses ask sb to do.

questions.question: Report the negative command.

options.text: He warned me not to touch it.
He warned me to not touched it.

questions.correct: Use not to + base verb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use not to + base verb.

narration.text:
祈使句表面没有主语，但命令或请求总是对某个人发出的。The teacher told us to sit down 中，us 就是原来被要求坐下的人，to sit down 是他们要执行的动作。转述时先找“让谁做什么”，再搭 tell 加人加 to do。<#0.8#>
She asked me to help her 不是一般疑问。原话里的 Please 表明请求，所以用 asked me to help；原说话人的 me 变为 her，因为现在是别人转述她的请求。ask 后的 me 是请求对象，不是被询问的问题答案。<#0.8#>
否定命令看 He warned me not to touch it。原来的否定祈使形式进入转述后，不保留 don’t，而把否定放在不定式前。报告动词还可以用 warned，说明这不只是普通命令，还带警告意味。操作顺序是：判断命令、请求还是警告；确定听话人；用合适的报告动词接人和不定式；否定词放在不定式标记前。

lessons.title: Reporting advice and suggestions
lessons.meta: advise sb to do; suggest doing/that-clause
examples: The doctor advised me to rest.
Mia suggested leaving early.
Mia suggested that we (should) leave early.
The evidence suggests that he was there.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: You should rest becomes advised me to rest; me is the addressee and to rest names the advised action.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: “Let’s leave early” becomes Mia suggested leaving early.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Mia suggested leaving early can expand to Mia suggested that we (should) leave early.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: shows may become suggests here without mandative grammar.

rules: advise + person + to do reports advice directed at someone.
suggest can take doing to propose an action.
suggest can take that + subject + (should) + base verb, but not suggest sb to do.
When suggest means “indicate”, its that-clause uses ordinary tense rather than mandative form.

questions.question: How can the advice be reported?

options.text: The doctor advised me to rest.
The doctor suggested me to rest.

questions.correct: advise sb to do is the correct pattern.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: advise sb to do is the correct pattern.

questions.question: Mia suggested ___ early.
questions.correct: suggest directly takes a gerund.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: suggest directly takes a gerund.

questions.question: Which is standard?

options.text: Mia suggested that we leave early.
Mia suggested us to leave early.

questions.correct: Do not use suggest sb to do.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Do not use suggest sb to do.

questions.question: The evidence suggests that he ___ there.
questions.correct: suggests means “indicates”, so use factual tense.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: suggests means “indicates”, so use factual tense.

narration.text:
“你应该休息”和“我们早点走吧”都像建议，但英语会根据有没有明确劝告对象选择不同骨架。The doctor advised me to rest 中，me 是医生劝的人，to rest 是劝我做的事，所以 advise 后可以接被劝的人和不定式。<#0.8#>
Mia suggested leaving early 不需要接一个被建议的人，suggest 后直接用 doing 表示建议的行动。也可以展开成页面第三句的 that 从句。注意 suggest 不能照搬 advise 的“人加不定式”结构。<#0.8#>
The evidence suggests that he was there 又不是“证据在提建议”。这里 suggests 表示“暗示、表明”，that 从句陈述证据指向的事实，因此用 was，不用建议性原形。判断时先看功能：对某人劝告，用 advise 人 to do；提出行动方案，用 suggest doing 或 suggest that 从句；主语是 evidence 一类事物时，suggest 往往表示暗示。

lessons.title: Reporting exclamations, greetings and responses
lessons.meta: Choose exclaim, greet, thank or agree by communicative function
examples: She exclaimed that the view was wonderful.
Tom thanked me for my help.
Mia promised to help.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The exclamative becomes a statement under exclaimed.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Thank you for your help becomes thanked me for my help; me is the person thanked and for my help gives the reason.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Here promised to help captures the commitment; if yes responded to an opinion, agreed might be appropriate instead.

rules: An exclamation may be reported with exclaim that... or paraphrased as a statement carrying the emotion.
Greetings, thanks and apologies should be reported by function rather than word-for-word form.
A yes/no response must be interpreted in context: yes may signal agreement, while I will may make a promise, so no single word has a mechanical conversion.

questions.question: Report the exclamation.

options.text: She exclaimed that the view was wonderful.
She asked if the view was wonderful.

questions.correct: Use exclaim + that statement.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use exclaim + that statement.

questions.question: Report the thanks.

options.text: Tom thanked me for my help.

questions.correct: Use thank sb for sth.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use thank sb for sth.

questions.question: Someone asked Mia for help and she replied, “Yes, I will help.” What is the most natural report?

options.text: Mia asked whether she should help.

questions.correct: In response to a request, I will help commits Mia to a future action.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: In response to a request, I will help commits Mia to a future action.

narration.text:
有些原话不是普通陈述，而是在感叹、道谢或答应。转述时要保留它完成的交际动作，不必复制原来的句型。She exclaimed that the view was wonderful 把原话的强烈感受保留下来，但嵌入 that 从句后，语序回到普通陈述顺序，不再保留感叹句外形。<#0.8#>
Tom thanked me for my help 直接按“道谢”这个功能转述。thanked 表明动作是感谢，me 是被感谢的人，for my help 说明感谢原因。逐词写 said that 并不能同样清楚地表现这个功能。<#0.8#>
Mia promised to help 则把一句肯定回应理解为“答应提供帮助”。如果肯定回应是在同意一个观点，报告动词可能是 agreed；如果是承诺去做事，就用 promise 接不定式。选择时别只看原话表面，要问说话人在做什么：感叹用 exclaimed，道谢用 thanked，承诺用 promised，同意观点用 agreed。

lessons.title: Backshift from present forms
lessons.meta: Present simple, continuous and perfect
examples: She said that she liked tea.
He said that he was working.
Mia said that she had finished.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I like tea becomes she liked tea by one-step backshift.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I am working becomes he was working, retaining progressive aspect.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I have finished becomes she had finished, retaining perfect aspect.

rules: Under a past reporting verb, present simple commonly backshifts to past simple.
Present continuous commonly backshifts to past continuous.
Present perfect commonly backshifts to past perfect.

questions.question: How is it commonly reported after said?
questions.correct: like commonly backshifts to liked.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: like commonly backshifts to liked.

questions.question: Report the sentence.
questions.correct: am working backshifts to was working.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: am working backshifts to was working.

questions.question: Report the sentence.
questions.correct: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect.

narration.text:
过去的某个时刻说了一句话，后来再报告时，原话的现在通常要跟着报告时间向过去移动。She said that she liked tea 中，原话用一般现在时表达喜好；后来用 said 回看，I 变 she，like 变 liked。<#0.8#>
He said that he was working 保留了“正在进行”的画面。原来的 am working 不是简单变成 worked，而是把现在进行时整体后移成过去进行时 was working，进行意义没有丢。<#0.8#>
Mia said that she had finished 中，原来的 have finished 已经表达“完成”，后移后成为 had finished，完成体仍然保留，只是参照点移到过去。可以把它们看成整套系统移动：一般现在到一般过去，现在进行到过去进行，现在完成到过去完成。先辨认原时态表达的状态、进行或完成，再把时间层级后移，不能只盯着单个动词词形。

lessons.title: Backshift from past and future forms
lessons.meta: Past, past continuous, will and be going to
examples: He said that he had lost the key.
She said that she had been waiting.
Tom said that he would call.

analyses.text: that he had lost the key.
analyses.label: Object clause (reported content)

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I lost the key becomes he had lost the key, locating the loss before the report.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I was waiting becomes she had been waiting, retaining progression.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I will call becomes he would call, future viewed from a past reporting point.

rules: Past simple commonly backshifts to past perfect, especially when sequence needs clarification.
Past continuous commonly backshifts to past perfect continuous.
will commonly becomes would; am/is/are going to commonly becomes was/were going to.

questions.question: What is the standard backshift?
questions.correct: lost backshifts to had lost.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: lost backshifts to had lost.

questions.question: What is the backshifted form?
questions.correct: was waiting backshifts to had been waiting.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: was waiting backshifts to had been waiting.

questions.question: Report the sentence.
questions.correct: will becomes would and call remains base form.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: will becomes would and call remains base form.

narration.text:
报告过去和将来时，关键是站到过去的报告点重新看时间。He said that he had lost the key 中，丢钥匙发生在 he said 之前。原话用一般过去时，后来的转述改用 had lost，把“更早发生”标清楚。<#0.8#>
She said that she had been waiting 保留了原来 was waiting 的持续过程，同时用 had been waiting 表示这段等待早于报告发生。不是所有过去动作都随便加 had，而是要让两个过去时间的先后清楚。<#0.8#>
Tom said that he would call 则把 will call 放到过去报告点之后。对 Tom 当时来说是将来，对现在的转述者来说是“过去所设想的将来”，所以 will 变 would。画一条时间线会更直观：早于过去报告点，用过去完成；原来在过去持续，用过去完成进行保留过程；晚于过去报告点的将来，用 would。

lessons.title: Modal changes in reported speech
lessons.meta: can, may, must and modals that often remain unchanged
examples: She said that she could swim.
He said that he had to leave.
Mia said that we should wait.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: I can swim becomes she could swim, retaining ability.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: must leave now becomes had to leave then.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: You should wait becomes she said that we should wait, retaining should.

rules: can commonly becomes could, and may commonly becomes might.
must often becomes had to for past obligation, but commonly remains must for logical deduction.
could, would, should and might normally do not backshift further, though meaning must be checked.

questions.question: Report the sentence.
questions.correct: can backshifts to could.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: can backshifts to could.

questions.question: How is past obligation commonly reported?
questions.correct: There is no musted; use had to for past obligation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: There is no musted; use had to for past obligation.

questions.question: What normally happens to should?
questions.correct: should normally remains unchanged.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: should normally remains unchanged.

narration.text:
情态动词转述时，既要看时间变化，也要保留原来的能力、必要性或建议意味。She said that she could swim 中，原话 can swim 表能力；在过去的 said 后，can 常变 could，能力这个意思仍然存在。<#0.8#>
He said that he had to leave 表达原话中“现在必须离开”的意思。must 在这里表示当时的必要，后来报告时常用 had to；表示“现在”的时间词若离开原现场，也会调整为 then。变化的不只是一个情态词，而是整段必要性和时间指向。<#0.8#>
Mia said that we should wait 中，should 通常不需要变化，因为它本身已表达建议或应当，转述后继续用 should 就能保留原意。不能把所有情态动词都机械后移。先判断情态意义：can 表能力常变 could；must 表当时义务常变 had to；should、might、could 等形式往往保持。最终还要结合语境，看它说的是能力、义务、推测还是建议。

lessons.title: Core boundaries where backshift is unnecessary
lessons.meta: General truths, still-valid content and immediate reporting
examples: The teacher said that water boils at 100°C.
Mia said that she lives in Shanghai.
He says that he is tired.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Although said is past, the general truth water boils... does not backshift.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Choose lives or lived according to whether the fact still holds.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: After says, retain is tired and change only person.

rules: General truths and scientific facts normally retain present simple.
If the content is still true at reporting time, present tense may remain; backshift can still neutrally report the past statement.
Immediate reporting or a present reporting verb normally does not trigger backshift.

questions.question: What is normally retained?
questions.correct: The scientific fact remains true.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The scientific fact remains true.

questions.question: If Mia still lives in Shanghai, what is possible?

options.text: Mia said that she lives in Shanghai.

questions.correct: Still-valid content may retain lives.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Still-valid content may retain lives.

questions.question: Report the present statement.

options.text: He says that he is tired.
He says that he was tired only.

questions.correct: Present-tense says normally causes no backshift.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Present-tense says normally causes no backshift.

narration.text:
时态后移是帮助时间关系清楚，不是只要看到 said 就把所有现在时变过去。The teacher said that water boils at 100°C 中，水在一百摄氏度沸腾是普遍事实，不只在老师说话那一刻成立，所以 boils 可以保留一般现在时。<#0.8#>
Mia said that she lives in Shanghai 取决于现实。如果转述时她仍住在上海，保留 lives 能强调情况现在有效；如果只忠实站在过去报告点，或现在情况未知，也可能用 lived。lived 本身不自动证明她现在已经搬走。<#0.8#>
He says that he is tired 更直接：报告动词 says 在现在，内容也处于当前视点，is tired 通常无需后移。判断是否后移时问三件事：报告动词是在过去还是现在；内容是不是客观事实；内容到转述时是否仍然成立。时态选择服务于真实时间关系，不能让变化表替你猜现实。

lessons.title: Changes in personal, possessive and reflexive pronouns
lessons.meta: Rebuild reference from speaker, addressee and referent
examples: Mia said that she was ready.
Tom told me that I was late.
Mia said that she had lost her key herself.

analyses.text: that she had lost her key herself.
analyses.label: Object clause (reported content)

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Identify original speaker Mia before selecting she.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Use the addressee in told me to resolve You as I.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: With I→she, change my→her and myself→herself consistently.

rules: First-person forms change according to the original speaker, not automatically from I to he.
Second-person forms change according to the original addressee and may become I, we, he, she or they.
Possessive and reflexive forms must agree with the newly resolved referent.

questions.question: Mia says “I am ready.” What does I become?
questions.correct: I refers to original speaker Mia.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: I refers to original speaker Mia.

questions.question: Tom says to me, “You are late.” What does You become?
questions.correct: You refers to the original addressee, me.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: You refers to the original addressee, me.

questions.question: Mia says “I lost my key myself.” What do my/myself become?
questions.correct: Both refer back to Mia.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Both refer back to Mia.

narration.text:
代词转换不是 I 永远变 she、you 永远变 I，而是重新确认每个词指谁。Mia said that she was ready 中，原话 I 指说话人 Mia，离开引号后用第三人称提到她，所以变 she。先找人物，再选代词，顺序不能倒。<#0.8#>
Tom told me that I was late 展示了 you 的变化。原话中的 you 指当时的听话人；报告句用 told me 明确这个听话人就是现在的 me，因此从句里写 I was late。换一个转述者或听话人，结果可能不同。<#0.8#>
Mia said that she had lost her key herself 中，一整套指代要同步：I 对应 she，my 对应 her，myself 对应 herself。反身代词必须跟它所强调或回指的人保持一致。处理时先列出原说话人、原听话人和现在报告者，再逐个问 I、you、my、your、myself 分别指谁；不要按表格孤立替换，否则很容易出现 she 丢了 my key 这类人物关系错误。

He said that he would leave the next day.

rules: this/these often become that/those when distance changes, but may remain if the referent is still present.
now, today, yesterday and tomorrow commonly become then, that day, the day before and the next/following day.
here often becomes there and come may become go when the directional viewpoint changes, but actual reporting location controls the choice.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Both directional and locative viewpoints shift.

narration.text:
this、tomorrow、here、come 都依赖说话现场。现场一换，它们才可能变化。She said that she liked that book 中，原来的 this book 是米娅当时手边或眼前的书；后来从较远的报告点提起，近指 this 变成 that。若转述者仍拿着同一本书，this 也可能保留。<#0.8#>
He said that he would leave the next day 把原话中的将来动作放到过去报告点重新定位。will 变 would，tomorrow 不再是报告者的明天，而是他说话后的第二天，所以写 the next day。<#0.8#>
Mia said that she would go there 中，原来的 come here 以米娅说话地点为中心；转述者不在那个地点时，方向变 go，地点变 there。判断这些词时要先标四个坐标：谁在说、哪一天说、在哪里说、后来在哪里报告。只有坐标真的移动，this、tomorrow、here、come 才需要相应调整。

groups.title: Advanced · 5 challenge lessons
groups.copy: Handle reporting-clause position, reverse restoration, layered reports, ambiguity and integrated rewriting.

lessons.title: Reporting-clause position and punctuation
lessons.meta: Initial, final and medial reporting clauses
examples: The notice read: "Keep out."
"I am ready," Mia said.
"If you hurry," she said, "you can catch it."

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: An initial reporting clause establishes the source before the quotation.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: When combining the quotation with final Mia said, change the full stop to a comma.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The reporting clause splits but does not syntactically break the original sentence.

rules: An initial reporting clause introduces the quotation with a comma, or a colon in some formal styles.
With a final reporting clause, a quoted statement normally ends with a comma before said + subject.
A medial reporting clause is set off by paired punctuation while the quotation remains one continuous sentence.

questions.question: What can introduce a quotation in a formal notice?
questions.correct: A colon may introduce the quotation in formal writing.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A colon may introduce the quotation in formal writing.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.correct: A quoted statement normally uses a comma before the final reporting clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A quoted statement normally uses a comma before the final reporting clause.

questions.question: What is needed around a medial reporting clause?
questions.correct: Paired commas mark the insertion.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Paired commas mark the insertion.

narration.text:
报告语可以放在原话前、后或中间，位置一变，标点也要跟着变。The notice read: "Keep out." 先交代文字来源，再用冒号引出完整内容。冒号像是在说“后面就是通知的原文”，引号内 Keep 首字母大写。<#0.8#>
"I am ready," Mia said 把原话放在前面。原话本来以句号结束，但后面还要接 Mia said，所以引号内先用逗号衔接，整个句子的句号放在报告语末尾。<#0.8#>
"If you hurry," she said, "you can catch it." 把报告语插进同一句原话中。she said 两边用成对逗号标出插入边界；后半句 you 不大写，因为拿掉中间报告语后，原话在语法上仍是一句连续的话。检查时先把报告语暂时拿掉，确认引号内原句是否完整，再按前置、后置或中置选择冒号、逗号和大小写。

lessons.title: Changing indirect speech back to direct quotation
lessons.meta: Reconstruct the speech situation, not mechanical reverse replacement
examples: Mia said, "I am tired."
He asked, "Where do you live?"
She said that she was pleased.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Returning from she to Mia’s viewpoint allows I, but this is a possible reconstruction, not proof of exact wording.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: where I lived has embedded statement order; in the original situation where he addressed me, one possible question is Where do you live?

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Distinguish grammatical restoration from uniquely recovering exact original words.

rules: When restoring direct speech, recover quotation marks, sentence type and the original speaker’s viewpoint; however, reported speech rarely proves the exact original wording.
When reconstructing one possible original question, restore question structure and the question mark, and resolve you from the original addressee.
Indirect speech may lose exact wording, so unique restoration is possible only with sufficient context.

questions.question: What is one possible original quotation for “Mia said that she was tired”?
questions.correct: If Mia spoke about herself, she used I, though the exact adjective might have differed.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: If Mia spoke about herself, she used I, though the exact adjective might have differed.

questions.question: What is one possible original question for “He asked where I lived”?
questions.correct: The direct wh-question restores do-support, you and the question mark.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The direct wh-question restores do-support, you and the question mark.

questions.question: Can we know uniquely whether the original used happy or pleased?
questions.correct: Indirect speech preserves meaning, not necessarily exact wording.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Indirect speech preserves meaning, not necessarily exact wording.

narration.text:
把间接引语还原成直接引语，做的是“重建一种可能的说话现场”，不是把变化表倒着走。先看 Mia said, "I am tired."。这是从转述内容恢复出的一种可能原话，原来指 Mia 的 she 回到她自己口中成为 I，同时恢复引号、首字母和句末标点。<#0.8#>
He asked, "Where do you live?" 展示疑问句的恢复。转述内容原本使用陈述语序；回到直接问句后，需要恢复 do 支持、原听话人的 you 和问号。<#0.8#>
但 She said that she was pleased 无法证明原话一定用了 pleased，也可能说 happy 或其他相近表达。间接引语保存的是意思，不一定保存精确词语。因此还原时把信息分两类：人称、句型、语序和标点可以按场景重建；原来的具体用词若没有证据，只能给出一种合理可能，不能声称唯一答案。

lessons.title: Layered reporting and temporal viewpoints
lessons.meta: Each layer has its own reporter, addressee and time center
examples: Tom said that Mia had told him that she was leaving.
She said that he had claimed that he had finished.

exampleNotes.body: First report Mia’s words, then embed that report under Tom said.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Backshift is finite; do not mechanically add another had.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus

rules: In layered reporting, start with the innermost speech and resolve person and tense one layer at a time.
An outer past report does not cause unlimited backshift; forms already in past perfect normally remain.
Repeated he/she/they in layered reporting can create reference ambiguity; repeat names when necessary.

questions.correct: The inner speaker and time anchor the outer transformation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The inner speaker and time anchor the outer transformation.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Past perfect normally does not backshift further.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Explicit names remove layered reference ambiguity.

narration.text:
多层转述像一段话经过两个人传递，每一层都有自己的“谁对谁说、在什么时候说”。Tom said that Mia had told him that she was leaving 中，先看最里面：Mia 对 Tom 说她要离开；再把这件事放进 Tom said。him 指 Tom，she 指 Mia，必须逐层确认。<#0.8#>
She said that he had claimed that he had finished 说明时态后移有终点。内层 had finished 已经是过去完成，外面再加一层过去报告时，通常仍保留这个形式，不继续机械叠加助动词。<#0.8#>
Tom said that Leo had told Tom that Leo was ready 看起来重复姓名，却比连续使用两个 he 更清楚。若全部换成代词，最后一个 he 可能指 Tom，也可能指 Leo。多层转述优先保证指代清晰，必要时重复姓名。分析时从最内层向外，每加一层就重新核对说话人、听话人、时间点和代词指向。

lessons.title: Ambiguity and meaning boundaries
lessons.meta: Tense, reference and reporting verbs all affect interpretation
examples: Mia said that she lived in Shanghai.
He admitted that he was wrong.
She refused to answer.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Do not infer present truth solely from a backshifted form.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Replacing said with admitted adds a stance of concession.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The refusal need not be copied word for word; to answer complements refused and preserves the communicative function.

rules: Past simple under a past reporting verb may be backshifted and does not necessarily mean the content is no longer true.
Reporting verbs encode stance: admit concedes, claim asserts and deny rejects; they are not interchangeable.
Indirect reporting may paraphrase rather than copy; judge rewrites by meaning, time and communicative function.

questions.question: Does it necessarily mean she no longer lives there?
questions.correct: lived may be only tense backshift.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: lived may be only tense backshift.

questions.question: What does admitted mean?
questions.correct: admit carries a conceding stance.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: admit carries a conceding stance.

questions.question: Can it be functionally reported as “She refused to answer”?
questions.correct: It preserves the communicative act of refusal.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It preserves the communicative act of refusal.

narration.text:
转述句语法正确，不等于意思已经唯一。Mia said that she lived in Shanghai 中，lived 可能只是因为 said 触发了时态后移，并不能单独证明她现在不住上海。要判断当前真假，还需要时间背景或其他语境。<#0.8#>
He admitted that he was wrong 与普通的 said 不同。admitted 不只报告内容，还加入“承认原本不愿接受的事实”这种立场。换成 claimed、denied，读者对说话人态度的理解会完全变化，所以报告动词本身也是意义的一部分。<#0.8#>
She refused to answer 则把原话中明确拒绝回答的交际功能直接概括出来，没有假装逐字复述。判断转述是否准确，要同时看三层：时态形式是否只是后移，代词是否有多个可能指向，报告动词是否增添了合适立场。间接引语允许意译，但时间、人物关系和原来的交际功能不能被改掉。

lessons.title: Integrated reported-speech rewriting
lessons.meta: Check sentence type, verb pattern, order, tense and reference together
examples: The doctor advised me not to work too late.
Mia asked why I had not called her the day before.
Leo suggested that we meet there the next day.

exampleNotes.body: Identify advice first, then use advised me not to work; me is the addressee and not to work... is the advised action.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: The suggestion becomes suggested that we meet there the next day, with verb pattern and deixis checked.

rules: The first integrated step is identifying communicative function to choose a frame such as say, ask, tell, advise or suggest.
Second, restore statement order in the embedded clause, then adjust tense and person.
Finally check five things: linker, reporting-verb pattern, statement order, temporal viewpoint and reference clarity.

why I had not called her

questions.wrong: Check the rule: An indirect question uses statement order.

narration.text:
综合改写不要同时乱改所有词，先决定原话在完成什么任务。The doctor advised me not to work too late 来自劝告，核心不是普通“说”，而是医生劝我别工作太晚，所以选 advise 接人和否定不定式。me 是劝告对象，后面的部分是行动内容。<#0.8#>
Mia asked why I had not called her the day before 来自特殊疑问。why 保留，原问句恢复陈述语序；me 按原说话人变 her，yesterday 随报告时间变 the day before。<#0.8#>
Leo suggested that we meet there the next day 来自邀请大家第二天在这里见面。suggest 使用 that 从句，不能套用“人加不定式”；here 和 tomorrow 是否变 there、the next day，要看报告地点和时间。完整检查可以按顺序进行：先判交际功能并选报告动词，再选 that、if、whether 或疑问词，恢复陈述语序，调整时间与人称，最后检查动词搭配和指代是否清楚。
